observation.visible_scene: A first-person, wide-angle view over a calm open sea under a bright low sun (sunrise/sunset) with thin high clouds. The white pointed nose of a surfboard occupies the lower-center of the frame, and a small low landmass sits on the right horizon. The viewpoint glides forward across the water surface.
visible_changes: At the start (t=0.00-0.20 s) the view is heavily distorted and blurred by water droplets and splashes on the lens, with the sun as a bright glare; the scene is largely obscured.
From about t=0.27 s onward the droplets thin out and the sea, horizon and sun become clearly visible, with only scattered residual water specks on the lens.
A white, pointed board nose rises into the bottom of the frame around t=0.87-1.2 s and then remains fixed at the lower center as the viewpoint moves steadily forward over the water.
A low strip of land on the right horizon becomes visible and persists through the later frames.
From t=2.2 s a right hand emerging from a black sleeve enters the right edge and paddles through the surface, kicking up small splashes, while the board nose stays centered.
Throughout, the sun's reflection streaks across the water on the left, and the overall brightness and cloud pattern stay consistent.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the initial water-on-lens distortion (submersion, wipeout, or spray) is not shown.
Whether the rider is paddling out, sitting on the board, or riding a wave is not determinable from the excerpt.
Events before t=0 and after the final frame are unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact distinction between camera tilt and board pitch as the nose enters view is not certain.
The white object is inferred to be a surfboard nose from shape and context but is not explicitly labeled.
Small water specks on the lens may be misread as distant objects.
